insider_details.detail: Two legal moments carry the script: the celebrant's monitum before the vows and each partner's vow line. Everything else (welcome, readings, ring exchange, story) is free to write. Build the personal script around those two blocks rather than squeezing them in at the end.

Choose two witnesses who are clearly over 18 and will be standing close by the whole time, not the person running the music or the photographer. They must be present for the monitum and vows and sign all 3 certificates straight after.

For couples flying home for a wedding, the in-person meeting with each partner and the NOIM timing (at least 1 month, not more than 18 months) mean the legal part has to be planned before the script. Lodge the NOIM from overseas if needed and book the separate in-person meetings into the trip home.

Build a signing table pause into the run sheet and have the celebrant check names and details on the certificates before guests leave: corrections can only be made while the couple and witnesses are still there.

A script with the Australian legal wording does not make a ceremony overseas legal. An Australian celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas, so couples marrying abroad either follow the destination's own law or sign legally at home and keep the overseas ceremony symbolic.
